question.prompt: A box contains \(5\) chips, numbered \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) and \(5.\) Chips are drawn randomly one at a time without replacement until the sum of the values drawn exceeds \(4.\) What is the probability that \(3\) draws are required?

solutions.title: Count the first two chips
solutions.explanation:
Any three distinct chips have sum at least \(1+2+3=6>4\). Thus exactly three draws are needed if and only if the first two chips have sum at most \(4\).

Imagine arranging all five chips randomly before applying the stopping rule. There are \(5\cdot4=20\) equally likely ordered pairs in the first two positions. This includes arrangements beginning with \(5\), even though the actual drawing would stop after that first chip.

A pair with sum at most \(4\) must contain \(1\), since otherwise its sum is at least \(2+3=5\). The other chip must be \(2\) or \(3\). Therefore the favorable ordered pairs are exactly
\[
(1,2),\quad(2,1),\quad(1,3),\quad(3,1).
\]
The probability is
\[
\frac{4}{20}=\boxed{\frac15},
\]
which is choice \(\text{D}\).
